clue.text: The number in the river, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver to go by how the river's name sounds when spoken

parts.note: the Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and western England

explanation.surface: A figure supposedly found in the river, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals the sound-alike: SEVERN, said quickly, sounds like the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, one more than six.

clue.text: The man's content in charge, though there's some animosity

indicators.note: content read as 'contents', so the man's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the man is a male

explanation.surface: A man in charge whose satisfaction is tinged with ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like contentment, but it is read as the contents of the man, with 'in charge' sitting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will or a wish to harm, a form of hostility.

clue.text: They feel for 26

parts.note: 26 across is the spotted six-legged insect; these are the sensory organs on its head it uses for touching its surroundings

explanation.surface: Sympathisers with a fellow crossword answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feel for' suggests sympathy, but it means literally probing by touch, as an insect's feelers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects carry a pair of sensory feelers on the head, used to touch and smell.

clue.text: Post requiring erudition?

definitions.meaning: post is mail, the items sent through the postal service
a man of ... is a learned person, so the word can mean scholarly learning

explanation.surface: A job in the mail service asks for scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail consists of written missives, while learning or literature is also called this, as in 'a man of' them.

clue.text: He'll sell about a thousand back and give voice after

indicators.note: after places the singing word behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: back says the short word for about is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to chant is to sing or give voice

explanation.surface: A seller who haggles over a thousand, then shouts his wares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the short word for about, putting ER after M; 'after' then places the singing word at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who sells goods for profit.

clue.text: Maybe let assets go to get flat

indicators.note: go here means go wrong or fall apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that allowing one's possessions to be sold leaves life dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is the anagram signal on LET ASSETS; 'Maybe' and 'to get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or a drink with no flavour is insipid, lacking any savour.

clue.text: What prompts one to go without a rest

indicators.note: to go without means to sit outside, so the prompting word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: a reminder is something that prompts one to remember

explanation.surface: Something that urges a person to carry on without taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go without' looks like doing without, but it means placing outside: REMINDER goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the leftover part, the balance after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Away to stop bread deteriorating

indicators.note: deteriorating means going to pieces, so the letters of the loaf word fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A method of keeping bread from going stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away', probably 'A way' run together in print, is a link before the definition 'stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone formally is to prevent or prohibit them from doing something.

clue.text: More sign

definitions.meaning: more as in additionally, in addition

explanation.definitionFit: In addition is one meaning, and the cross-shaped symbol in sums is the other.

clue.text: Holding money in America, sent a deposit

indicators.note: holding means the word sent wraps around the coin

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Keeping cash in the United States, someone sent off a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests a bank payment, but it is the silt that settles out of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt or grounds settling at the bottom of a liquid form a layer of matter laid down.

clue.text: Company returns in modern place

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round company abbreviation inside the word for modern

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late developments'

indicators.note: returns means the company's short form is read backwards

explanation.surface: A firm comes back into a contemporary setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reads the company abbreviation backwards; LATE for modern is a common crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: To position or find the site of something is to fix its whereabouts.

clue.text: Heel reading French article first, then English

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'
an is the English indefinite article, 'article' carried over from the French one

explanation.surface: A scoundrel studies a French piece of writing before an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' is not a foot or a cad: it means to tilt, as a ship heels over. 'article' serves both languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels tilts to one side, which is to tip or incline.

clue.text: Making all cry, as really wretched

indicators.note: making means forming something new out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something so miserable that it reduces everyone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is the anagram signal on ALL CRY AS; 'really' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguish and mean, behaving like a scoundrel, is contemptible.

clue.text: Those caps adapted to fit a Continental gun

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of these words are reworked

explanation.surface: Headgear modified to suit a European firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges THOSE CAPS; 'to fit' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a French breech-loading rifle of the 1860s, so a weapon from mainland Europe.

clue.text: The child prepared to fight won

parts.note: someone armed carries weapons and is ready for battle

explanation.surface: A youngster ready for battle came out victorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won' is not victory but 'won over', delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone won over is captivated or delighted.

clue.text: The individual making out his property has been sold

definitions.text: The individual making out his property has been sold

parts.words: The individual making out his property has been sold
parts.note: making out means understanding, and also converting property into cash by selling it; the person doing either

explanation.surface: Someone discovering that their belongings have been sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making out' can mean grasping a fact, and to sell property is to turn assets into money.
explanation.definitionFit: One who comes to understand something, or one who converts assets into cash.

clue.text: Argue for check-up

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a test is an examination or check

explanation.surface: Two cases presented: making a case for a medical examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To object or remonstrate is to assert or contend against something.

clue.text: Living with discord engulfing the party

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the word for discord wraps around the party

parts.note: a rent is a split or rift, as in a schism
a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Coexisting amid strife that has swallowed the political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration, but it means one side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dwelling in a place makes their home there.

clue.text: One of the family assuming a right which is questionable

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative claiming an entitlement that is open to doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assuming' means taking on, so A and R follow UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doubtful or uncertain is not clear-cut.

clue.text: Criminal beast repeatedly put inside

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for the beast is written twice in a row

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a beast of burden
someone put inside is in, in prison

explanation.surface: An animal criminal keeps getting jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' looks like a container signal, but it means jailed, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer or murderer is a lawbreaker of the worst kind.

clue.text: A store only half-finished

indicators.note: only half says to keep just one half of the word finished, here its second part

explanation.surface: A shop that is still being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-finished' looks like a building site; take the back half of FINISHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut is a simple storage building.

clue.text: Certain to be in the treasurer's safe

indicators.note: to be in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The money must surely be inside the treasurer's strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' suggests the strongbox, but it is just part of the run the letters sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being positive or confident about something means being in no doubt.

clue.text: Beer at fault? Discount that

indicators.note: at fault read as letters gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Faulty beer should earn a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' rearranges BEER AT; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction or partial refund on a price is a deduction.

clue.text: Quarrel with Cockney school!

indicators.note: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English private school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A row with a London school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' is not a row: it is the bolt fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow bolt is a type of missile shot from a bow.

clue.text: A red church tower

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to tower is to rise high

explanation.surface: A crimson steeple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is a verb, to soar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry-coloured shade is a bright pinkish crimson.

clue.text: A six-footer spotted this pen possibly

definitions.meaning: a six-legged insect with spots on its back
a pen is a female swan, so a bird that is a lady

explanation.surface: Seeing a tall man, this writing instrument perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means six legs; a 'pen' is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spotted beetle, and a female bird such as a swan.

clue.text: It's disheartening!

parts.note: read literally as removing the heart, as a kitchen tool takes out the middle of an apple

explanation.surface: An exclamation of discouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' means removing hearts, not discouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool that removes the centre of fruit takes out its heart.

clue.text: Many on a train may appear in the pink

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many

indicators.note: may appear signals the letters will show up in another form

explanation.surface: Lots of passengers aboard may look healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' looks like good health, but 'the pink' is the flower; 'may appear' is the anagram signal, and C (a hundred) for many is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are flowers of the Dianthus genus, close kin to this garden bloom.
